title: Open a query from a database span

blocks.content: This guide runs on your own stack. The steps that depend on your traces or on the link can be skipped if your traces have no suitable span or the link is not available on your stack.
To open a trace that contains a database span, complete the following steps:

blocks.title: Open a trace with a database span

blocks.content:
Select the **Database calls** primary signal.

**Go there** opens Traces Drilldown with **Database calls** selected. The signal sits in the dropdown next to **Root spans** and **All spans**, and it keeps only spans whose `db.system.name` attribute names a database system, so every trace listed contains a database span.

Check whether the panels show data.

**Database calls** matches the current OpenTelemetry attribute, `db.system.name`. Many applications still send the older `db.system` attribute, which the Database Observability link also accepts. If the panels show no data, complete the next step. If they show data, skip it.

Select **All spans** and filter on **span.db.system**.

**Go there** applies both: **All spans** as the primary signal, and a filter where **span.db.system** matches `mysql` or `postgresql`, the two database systems the link supports.
Set the time range to a period when your application ran database calls.

blocks.reftarget: [data-testid='grafana-exploretraces-app tab-trace-list'], [data-testid='data-testid Tab Traces'], [data-testid='data-testid Tab Errored traces'], [data-testid='data-testid Tab Slow traces']

blocks.content:
Click the name of a trace.

For example, pick a request you know touched the database, such as a page that lists records. If the list is empty, widen the time range and continue.
You opened a trace that contains a database span.
To open the query from its span, complete the following steps:

blocks.title: Open the query from the span

blocks.content:
Mark the database spans.

In **Filters** above the spans, add a **Text search** for `db.system`. Spans whose attributes contain `db.system` are highlighted, and the count next to the filter shows how many match.

Click a highlighted span.

Its details show a **Database** group with the database system and the query text.

Select the query text in the **Database** group.

The query text is the Database Observability link; it carries the Database Observability icon. If you do not see the link, skip this step and the next one.
blocks.tooltip: This opens the query in Database Observability.

blocks.content:
Select an instance.

This step can appear when more than one database instance contains the query. For example, the same query can run on a production and a staging server.

Where the link opens tells you whether the match found the query:

- **Query samples** tab: the match found the query. Record the query text.
- **Queries overview**: the match did not find the query. Record that no match was found.
